successCriteria.description: A new test case exists inside the existing `describe('periodContaining', ...)` block in tests/unit/shared/date.test.ts that calls `periodContaining(anchor, 0, date)` with a `date` at or after the shared anchor (e.g. `new Date(Date.UTC(2023, 0, 10))`) and asserts the call throws `ConflictError`.

The new test asserts the exact error message `'Unable to resolve accrual period'` (e.g. via `toThrow('Unable to resolve accrual period')` or an equivalent message assertion), matching the message thrown at src/shared/date/accrual.ts:37.

The full Jest suite passes (`npx jest`) with the new test included, and the new test exercises the 10,000-iteration loop-exhaustion path (accrualMonths = 0) rather than the earlier `'Requested date precedes the accrual anchor'` branch.

constraints: The new test must be added to the existing `describe('periodContaining', ...)` block in tests/unit/shared/date.test.ts and reuse the existing shared `anchor` constant; it must not modify production code in src/shared/date/accrual.ts.

The test must use `accrualMonths = 0` and a `date` at or after the anchor (e.g. `new Date(Date.UTC(2023, 0, 10))`) so it reaches the loop-exhaustion path rather than the `'Requested date precedes the accrual anchor'` branch.
The test must assert both the error type (`ConflictError`, imported from src/shared/errors) and the exact message `'Unable to resolve accrual period'`.
outOfScope: Changing the production implementation of `periodContaining` (e.g. adding an explicit guard for `accrualMonths <= 0`) is out of scope — this phase only adds a test documenting the existing behavior.
Adding tests for other `periodContaining` edge cases (negative accrualMonths, non-integer months, dates far beyond the anchor) is out of scope for this phase.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The asserted error message must exactly match the string literal thrown by `periodContaining` when the loop exhausts: `'Unable to resolve accrual period'`.
The test must import `periodContaining` from `src/shared/date` and `ConflictError` from `src/shared/errors`, matching the existing imports in the test file.
